_about: Hand-written reference answers, one per case, written from the frozen DATA blocks. They are what a correct answer looks like and are used to prove the checks pass good output (providers/reference.mjs) and catch seeded faults (providers/faulty.mjs). They are not used to grade live answers.

T01.answer: Captain Mbeumo, but it is close to a coin flip. FixtureShark projects Mbeumo at 5.33 points at home to Tottenham and Tavernier at 5.27 away at Chelsea, with Gibbs-White and Ødegaard on 5.05 each. The gap between the top two is 0.06 points, far smaller than a normal week's swing, so either of them is a reasonable choice. These are model estimates.

T02.answer: Barry. FixtureShark projects him at 6.02 points for GW6 away at Hull, ahead of Gonzalo on 4.92 and Kostoulas on 3.66. His expected goals are 0.698 against Gonzalo's 0.5 and Kostoulas's 0.345, and at £5.7m he costs less than Gonzalo (£6.1m). Kostoulas carries the most minutes risk, with a 0.819 chance of starting against 0.944 for the other two. These are model estimates.

T03.answer: Man City have the best attacking fixtures from GW7 to GW10, and both models agree: they average 2.21 expected goals a game on the market and 2.38 on Dixon-Coles, the highest of the six on each. Arsenal are second on both (2.12 and 1.49). FPL's FDR disagrees: it rates Fulham's run as the easiest, at an average of 2.5, but the market expects Fulham to score only 1.53 a game and Dixon-Coles 1.2, so their easy FDR reflects weaker opponents rather than many goals for Fulham. Goal figures are model estimates.

Man City average Dixon-Coles goals GW7-10

T04.answer: Tavernier (£6.1m) and Ødegaard (£6.8m): £12.9m in total for 10.32 projected points (5.27 + 5.05). The next best pair within budget is Tavernier and Groß, 9.98 points for £12.0m. These are model estimates for GW6.

T05.answer: Tzolis is out: he is injured (hamstring, expected back 24 Oct) and the model gives him no chance of starting. The other three are doubtful with a 75% chance of playing according to FPL's news. The model rates Rice the most likely to start (0.728), then Havertz (0.708) and Konsa (0.675), but Havertz has the highest projection at 3.93 points, ahead of Konsa on 2.99 and Rice on 2.84. FPL's own chance-of-playing field is blank for all four, so the 75% comes from the news text.
T05.recommendation: Havertz, Konsa and Rice may play; Tzolis will not

T07.answer: Decent short-term punt, not a long-term hold. Brobbey's hamstring has him expected back on 25 Oct, and our model has Isidor on 4.79 points in GW6 and 4.49 in GW7, with a 0.9 chance of starting. Once Brobbey is due back that drops sharply: 1.4 projected in GW8 and under a point a week after that (model estimates, not guarantees). So fine for a free transfer if you plan to move him on after GW7; just don't expect him to keep the shirt. Side by side here: https://fixtureshark.com/fpl/compare?players=wilson-isidor,brian-brobbey&from=6&to=10

T08.answer: No, not for a five-week hold. Calvert-Lewin is projected 0.97 points below Wissa in GW6, the move breaks even in GW8, and over GW6 to GW10 it gains 2.39 points, less than the 4-point hit. The cumulative gain only passes 4 in GW12 (6.36), so the hit pays only if you keep him that long. As a free transfer it would be worth making.
T08.recommendation: No: don't take the hit for a five-week hold

T09.answer: Not quite: it depends what you use it for. In FixtureShark's study, when comparing different players in the same week, an xG fixture rating picked the higher scorer 57.5% of the time against 55.6% for FDR, so xG is better there. But for timing the same player's weeks, FDR did better: 55.8% against 54.4% for xG. Market team goals beat both in each case (59.9% and 57.0%). So FDR isn't useless, and bookmakers' expected goals are the best guide of the three.
T09.recommendation: No: FDR still helps; market team goals are best

T10.answer: Saka, narrowly. FixtureShark projects Saka at 7.07 points at home to Leeds and Haaland at 6.55 away at Liverpool, a gap of 0.52, so this is close. The market gives City 1.67 goals at Anfield; Haaland has averaged 6.3 points a start when City's market goals were 1.5 to 2, and 5.68 in 22 starts away at the old big six, blanking in 11. Arsenal's market goals at home to Leeds are 2.09. Haaland is a reasonable pick, but Saka is slightly better on the numbers.
